## Brazil, Argentina and Chile in 15 days: why add a third country?

The route connects [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), Iguazu Falls, [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/). It suits travelers interested in South American urban culture, panoramic natural landscapes and the opportunity to add a wine region or the Pacific coast.

**The main difference from two-country programs is a dedicated finale in Chile.** The final days are spent in Santiago, making Chile a full part of the experience rather than a brief connection. This requires additional time for flights and travel between regions.

## Main stages of the journey

| Days | Planned activities |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Rio, Sugarloaf Mountain, Corcovado, city center |
| 5–7 | Brazilian and Argentine sides of Iguazu |
| 8–11 | Buenos Aires, tango, Tigre |
| 12–15 | Santiago, city sightseeing and free time |

In Rio, viewpoints reveal the coast, bay and built-up hillsides. The nature-focused stage then takes you through [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/): the Brazilian side offers sweeping views of the waterfalls, while the Argentine side has a different network of paths and viewpoints.

In Buenos Aires, the itinerary includes city excursions, tango and a visit to [Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/) among the river channels. Possible optional outings to a gaucho ranch or Montevideo do not mean that Uruguay forms part of the principal three-country itinerary.

## Santiago, Maipo and the Pacific coast

[Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) lies at the foot of the Andes and differs considerably from Rio and Buenos Aires geographically. After the city tour, you can choose how to spend your free time.

For visiting wineries, consider the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/). To see the ocean coast, look at [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/). Chile's official tourism portal groups the capital, wine valleys and coastal cities within one geographical destination, but each option has its own itinerary and duration.

Trips to Maipo and the coast can be arranged as extras. **They must not be assumed to be included in the price.** If you plan both, confirm the length of the outings and timing of the return flight in advance.

## Services and expenses: what to check before booking

The price includes accommodation in the listed hotels or similar properties, excursions with an **English-speaking guide**, and airport–hotel–airport transfers with a driver. Russian-speaking guiding in all three countries is not confirmed as part of these arrangements.

International and domestic air tickets, optional excursions and some meals are paid separately. Domestic flights are calculated separately; before paying, reconcile that estimate with the particular traveler's tickets and baggage. Early departures may affect the availability of hotel breakfast.

For the two sides of Iguazu, border documents and current trail access must also be checked. Temperatures, humidity and weather conditions may differ between Rio, the falls and central Chile, so pack for all stops rather than only the first city.

## Which other itinerary should you compare with this tour?

The [10-day private Brazil–Argentina tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-vip-10-days/) focuses on Rio, the waterfalls and Buenos Aires without Chile. The [14-day group Brazil–Argentina program](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-group-tour/) adds the Amazon and Salvador instead of Santiago.

Choose the 15-day option for Chile: then the final days in Santiago and the opportunity to visit the country's central regions become meaningful parts of the journey, rather than merely an extra stopover.

## Frequently asked questions about the three-country journey

### Are all three countries part of the main itinerary?

Yes: Brazil, Argentina and Chile. The visit to Montevideo is listed as an optional addition.

### Which language do the included guides speak?

The list of included services specifies English-speaking guides. Russian-speaking guidance can be discussed separately and should not be assumed to be included.

### Are the trips to Maipo and Valparaíso included?

They are presented as optional activities that must be arranged before booking.

### Are domestic flights included?

No. They are listed as separate expenses alongside international air tickets.

## Brazil–Argentina group tour in 14 days: what makes it different?

Unlike the shorter Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires route, this program visits several regions of Brazil. After [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), the journey continues to the [Amazon](/brazil/place/manaus-amazon/), then [Salvador](/brazil/place/salvador/), Iguazu Falls and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/).

This tour is intended for travelers who want to combine jungle, rivers, historic neighborhoods and famous attractions. Excursions operate **in a shared SIB group**, so their common departure schedule differs from private arrangements, which provide more flexibility in choosing when to make each stop.

## How the days and nights are allocated

| Days | Main itinerary |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | Rio: Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain, city center |
| 4–5 | Manaus, Amazon lodge |
| 6–8 | Salvador and [Praia do Forte](/brazil/place/praia-do-forte/) |
| 9–10 | Foz do Iguaçu, Brazilian waterfalls |
| 11–14 | Buenos Aires, city sightseeing and tango |

A total of 13 nights is planned: 3 in Rio, 2 in the Amazon, 3 in Salvador, 2 near Iguazu and 3 in Buenos Aires. There are several flights between regions. This is an important consideration for travelers who find frequent packing and hotel changes tiring.

## Two days in the Amazon: what is actually included?

Near Manaus, a river transfer is arranged to Evolução Ecolodge or an agreed equivalent. Activities include canoeing through flooded igapó forest, piranha fishing, a jungle walk and an introduction to local community life. **Full board** is included during the lodge stay.

In the evening, there may be an opportunity to explore the shoreline by spotlight, where caimans and other animals can be seen under suitable conditions. Sightings cannot be guaranteed: they depend on water levels, weather and animal behavior.

For this stage, prepare comfortable closed-toe shoes and clothes suitable for a humid climate, and clarify river-transport arrangements. Other nature-based options can be compared in the [nature and wildlife tours section](/interests/wildlife/).

## Salvador and time by the ocean

In [Salvador](/brazil/place/salvador/), the program explores Pelourinho, historic churches and Afro-Brazilian cultural heritage. The city was the first capital of Portuguese Brazil, and its historic center is on the UNESCO World Heritage List.

The following day is devoted to [Praia do Forte](/brazil/place/praia-do-forte/) and relaxing beside the ocean. This stop provides a change of pace after cultural excursions and before flying to Iguazu, but it does not turn the entire itinerary into an extended beach holiday.

## Which side of Iguazu Falls is included?

The itinerary includes **the Brazilian side of the waterfalls** near [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), with admission to the park listed among the included services. The Argentine side should not automatically be assumed to be part of the program simply because the next flight is to Argentina.

Travelers then fly to Buenos Aires, where a city sightseeing tour with a Russian-speaking guide, historic neighborhoods and a tango show with dinner are scheduled. There is also a free day for independent exploring.

If you want to visit both sides of the waterfalls, compare this itinerary with the [private 10-day VIP tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-vip-10-days/), which allocates a separate day to the Argentine park. The difference concerns the excursions included, not merely the level of service.

## What is included in the price and what is paid separately?

The group tour lists hotels or equivalent properties with breakfast, SIB excursions with Russian-speaking assistance, transfers, full board at the Amazon lodge, admission to the Brazilian waterfalls and dinner with a tango show. Different hotel categories and accommodation arrangements have separate rates.

**International and domestic air tickets are not included.** For the total budget, account for flights along the Rio–Manaus–Salvador–Foz do Iguaçu–Buenos Aires route, baggage rules, personal expenses and optional activities. Hotels may be replaced with comparable properties, while holiday and carnival dates require separate arrangements.

## Frequently asked questions about the group tour

### How does SIB differ from a private itinerary?

SIB refers to shared group excursions. The journey follows a common schedule rather than each traveler's individually customized timetable.

### How much time is spent in the Amazon?

Two nights at the lodge are planned, with river and nature activities. Full board is included during the stay.

### Will we visit Iguazu Falls from the Argentine side?

The page confirms a visit to the Brazilian side. The Argentine side needs to be discussed as a separate addition if it is essential to you.

### Are meals included throughout the route?

Breakfast is included at the hotels, full board at the Amazon lodge, and a tango-show dinner in Buenos Aires. Other meals should be checked day by day.

### Do flights between the cities need to be paid for?

Yes. Domestic air tickets are a separate expense, as is the international flight.

## New Year in Rio, Iguazu Falls and Buenos Aires in 10 days

The main event of this itinerary is **celebrating New Year's Eve on Copacabana Beach** in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). The journey begins on December 30, the festive night falls on December 31, and the program continues with Rio sightseeing, two days at Iguazu Falls and a finale in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/).

The full itinerary lasts **10 days and 9 nights, from December 30 through January 8**. The specific departure year is not stated here; the date and group availability must be confirmed when choosing the tour. One important feature is free time after the festivities and before the return flight, rather than nonstop morning excursions.

## Holiday days in Rio: how to avoid an exhausting schedule

December 30 includes an airport welcome, hotel transfer and free time. On December 31, a Russian-speaking guide leads an excursion to [Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado](/brazil/place/corcovado-christ-the-redeemer/), followed by an evening celebration beside the ocean at Copacabana.

January 1 features [Sugarloaf Mountain](/brazil/place/sugarloaf-mountain/) and an introduction to Rio's historic center. After a night of fireworks and mass celebrations, it is worth pacing yourself. **January 2 is a free day**, when you can relax by the ocean or choose an optional excursion. It provides a welcome break before the flights.

Travel around New Year's requires allowing for large crowds, street closures and traffic around the beach. The group's meeting point, return to the hotel and access to individual districts are arranged according to the actual organization of the celebration. Official event rules may change and cannot simply be inferred from the previous year's timetable.

## Two days at Iguazu: Brazil and Argentina

On January 3, the group flies from Rio to [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and checks into a hotel. **January 4** is devoted to the Brazilian side of the waterfalls, and **January 5** to the Argentine side from [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). A flight to Buenos Aires is planned after the second excursion day.

This sequence allows travelers to see the entire sweep of the falls first and then walk the boardwalks closer to the cascades and Devil's Throat. It is a protected natural area of humid subtropical forest, so closed-toe shoes with nonslip soles and protection from spray are useful.

Macuco Safari and the Bird Park are listed **as optional activities** on the Brazilian side, not as prepaid elements of the New Year package. Their cost and timing should be considered separately from the main excursion.

## Buenos Aires: city sightseeing, tango and a day of your choice

On January 6, a Russian-speaking guide leads a tour of the Argentine capital. The route includes La Boca, San Telmo, Plaza de Mayo, Recoleta and Puerto Madero. The program also features a tango show with dinner.

January 7 is free. You can explore the city further or choose a separate excursion to [Tigre](/argentina/place/tigre/), an experience of gaucho culture or a trip to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) across the Río de la Plata. All are optional. Visiting Uruguay means adding another country and checking documents for a separate border crossing; **the mandatory itinerary covers Brazil and Argentina**.

January 8 includes a transfer to Buenos Aires airport and departure. Unlike a short trip focused solely on celebrating in Rio, this route offers both sides of Iguazu Falls and a distinct cultural finale.

## What is included in the price and which expenses are additional?

The program starts **from $4373**. The price includes hotels along the route, scheduled group excursions with a Russian-speaking guide, group transfers with a driver and **domestic flights on the Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires route**.

International flights are paid separately. Optional excursions are also paid separately: the program lists Macuco Safari, the Bird Park, Tigre, the Montevideo trip and a gaucho fiesta, for example. Accommodation terms and the actual departure date must match the confirmed offer; the costs of optional programs must not automatically be added to the base price.

When comparing holiday itineraries, distinguish between [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) and [combined multi-country journeys](/multi-country/). The New Year program focuses on Copacabana and a relatively relaxed distribution of time. Other routes may allocate more days to nature reserves, active pursuits or individual regions.

## Frequently asked questions about the Brazil–Argentina New Year tour

### Where is New Year's Eve celebrated?

According to the itinerary, the festive night of December 31 takes place on Copacabana Beach in Rio de Janeiro.

### Is there time to rest after New Year's Eve?

Yes. January 2 is a free day in Rio, and another free day is scheduled in Buenos Aires on January 7.

### Do I need to purchase the domestic flights separately?

No. Flights on the Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires route are included in the published program. International tickets are paid separately.

### Can I visit a third country?

An optional trip to Montevideo is available, but Uruguay **is not part of the mandatory itinerary**. The trip's cost and border-crossing documents are arranged separately.

## Brazil, Argentina and Peru in 14 days: Iguazu, Machu Picchu and Titicaca

Over two weeks, the itinerary crosses three South American countries. The journey begins with the Atlantic Ocean and the mountains of [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), followed by Iguazu Falls on both sides of the border and the historic neighborhoods of Buenos Aires. In Peru, the program continues with Lima, Cusco, Machu Picchu and high-altitude Lake Titicaca.

This combination suits travelers who want to see **both famous natural landmarks and major monuments of Inca culture** on one trip. The trade-off for such a full itinerary is several flights, long transfers and a significant gain in altitude during the Peruvian stage. Travelers need to be comfortable changing accommodation regularly.

## Geography of the two-week itinerary

| Country | Main stops |
|---|---|
| Brazil | Rio, Iguazu |
| Argentina | Iguazu, Buenos Aires |
| Peru | Lima, Cusco, Titicaca |

In Rio, visits to Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and the city are scheduled. After flying to the Iguazu area, you visit [Foz do Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and the Argentine side via [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Then comes Buenos Aires, with historic districts and a tango show.

The flight to Peru changes the scenery: first [Lima](/peru/place/lima/) on the Pacific coast, then the mountains around [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/), and later the [Puno and Lake Titicaca area](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). As a result, you will see both the Atlantic and Pacific coasts as well as the high Andes.

## Rio and Iguazu Falls: a nature-filled beginning

Corcovado and Sugarloaf Mountain offer different views over Rio, its bay, urban beaches and granite peaks. The city stage is well suited to the first days: you can discover Brazilian culture before moving on to longer transfers.

At Iguazu Falls, the experience is divided between two sides. The Brazilian side offers sweeping panoramas of the cascades, while the Argentine side lets you follow paths closer to the powerful water flows and Devil's Throat. The program allows two days for this area, so visiting both sides is a different experience from a one-day excursion out of Rio.

Crossing the border depends on the traveler's documents and current conditions. Individual trails may occasionally close because of water levels or maintenance work; the Iguazu visit does not promise access to any specific boardwalk at a particular hour.

## Buenos Aires: history and tango

In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), sightseeing explores the historic neighborhoods of La Boca and San Telmo, squares and other well-known city locations. In the evening, the program includes a tango show with music and dinner. It offers a cultural contrast after the natural panoramas of Iguazu.

The capital stage is designed as an introduction to the city, not an independent in-depth exploration of all Argentina. Adding glaciers or Ushuaia would require a different itinerary and additional days.

## Peru: from Lima to Cusco and Machu Picchu

[Lima](/peru/place/lima/) introduces the architecture of its historic center and modern coastal districts. The itinerary includes Plaza Mayor, the Convent of San Francisco, Miraflores and the Larco Museum.

The journey then reaches Cusco, situated at approximately **3,400 metres above sea level**. In the city and its surroundings, you will see archaeological sites including Sacsayhuamán, Qenqo, Puka Pukara and Tambomachay. This heritage of the Inca world provides historical context for the next visit.

[Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) is a major destination in its own right. Entry to the archaeological complex depends on a confirmed ticket and authorized visiting route. Access to every section of the monument cannot be assumed: different areas are subject to their own regulations.

## Lake Titicaca and the altitude of the Andes

The Peruvian section concludes with a trip to [Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). Here you will encounter high-altitude nature and the cultural traditions of local communities. Compared with the earlier tropical and city days, this stage is particularly different in its weather, temperature and physical sensations.

The altitude of Cusco and the Titicaca region deserves attention. Travelers sensitive to rapid altitude gain should assess medical limitations and the possibility of acclimatization in advance. An extra acclimatization day cannot be added automatically without changing the total length of the itinerary, so this should be discussed when choosing the tour.

## Guide languages and transport

**Russian-speaking guides** are scheduled for excursions in Rio, Iguazu, Buenos Aires, Lima and the Cusco city tour. **English-speaking guides** accompany visits to Machu Picchu and Lake Titicaca. This distinction matters for travelers who would like Russian-language guidance at every stop.

Included services are hotel accommodation, scheduled excursions and group transfers with a driver. Optional excursions, international air tickets and **domestic flights from $950 per person** are paid separately. Meals and drinks beyond those specified in the program are also not included in the overall amount.

The tour price starts **from $6449**. Compare it with other tours taking domestic airfare, hotel category, transportation format and guiding language into account. The extensive geography requires a realistic budget for journeys between countries.

## Who should choose this tour?

The itinerary suits travelers who want to explore three countries in one trip and are prepared for long transfers and changes in altitude. Its central attraction is the combination of Brazil's and Argentina's natural landmarks with Peru's cultural heritage.

To compare options, explore [Peru tours](/peru/tour/), [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) and other [multi-country itineraries](/multi-country/). If Machu Picchu is your main goal and you are less interested in the waterfalls and Rio, a Peru-only program would allow more time for the Andes.

## Frequently asked questions about the 14-day tour

### Are all flights included in the price?

No. Domestic flights are paid separately, with a starting estimate of $950 per person, and international tickets are excluded from the base price as well.

### Is the entire program guided in Russian?

No. Russian-language guidance is specified for the main city excursions, but guides at Machu Picchu and Lake Titicaca speak English.

### Can I visit both sides of Iguazu Falls?

Yes. The itinerary includes the Brazilian and Argentine sides of the falls, with two days allocated to the area.

### Is the journey suitable for travelers who struggle with altitude?

The Peruvian section includes Cusco at around 3,400 metres and the high-altitude Titicaca region. If you have medical restrictions, discuss the suitability of this ascent with a doctor in advance and choose an appropriate travel pace.

## Rio Carnival, Iguazu and Buenos Aires in 10 days

This Ada Tours itinerary lasts **10 days and 9 nights**, visiting [Brazil](/brazil/) and [Argentina](/argentina/). You spend several days in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/), watch the Carnival parade at the Sambadrome, then travel to Iguazu Falls and finish in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/).

The main difference from an ordinary sightseeing trip is the nighttime samba-school parade, around which part of the stay in Rio is organized. The second major natural attraction is also significant: Iguazu Falls is visited **from both the Brazilian and Argentine sides**, which have different viewing paths and perspectives on the cascades.

## Rio de Janeiro before the Carnival parade

The first day is set aside for arrival, check-in and getting to know the city. A visit to Sugarloaf Mountain and a walk through Rio's old center follow. From the heights, you can see Guanabara Bay, ocean beaches and city neighborhoods set between granite hillsides.

On a separate day, you ascend Corcovado to the Christ the Redeemer statue. This viewpoint and Sugarloaf Mountain show Rio from different angles, which makes both excursions worthwhile in their own right.

The remaining time can be spent at Copacabana or Ipanema. However, rest before the Carnival evening is important: the principal parade takes place at night, and spectators spend several hours in the stands.

## The Sambadrome: what spectators will see

The Carnival parade takes place at the Sambadrome. Samba schools proceed along the specially prepared avenue with musicians, dancers, costumed groups and large decorative floats. Each school has its own theme, presentation and performance time.

For travelers, this is a rare opportunity to experience Carnival not only on the city streets but also as a major organized competition. **Carnival tickets are included in the tour price**, as is the hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfer.

However, seat type, exact sector, school performance times and the current parade calendar must be checked for the particular departure. The same lineup of schools and program cannot be promised every year.

## Iguazu: two countries and two experiences

After Rio, the route moves to [Iguazu on the Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/). Here, broad panoramas of the waterfalls are particularly impressive against the tropical forest. This is followed by a trip to the [Argentine side of Iguazu](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/), where walkways approach individual water flows more closely.

These are separate national parks on opposite sides of an international border. Border-crossing time, visiting routes and access to particular trails depend on current rules and conditions. Both sides are included in the main itinerary, rather than merely offered as possible extras.

## Buenos Aires: the city and tango

In Argentina, the journey continues to Buenos Aires. The itinerary includes a city sightseeing tour, visits to districts and squares, and **a tango show with dinner**. One day is left free for independent museum visits, neighborhood walks or an additional activity.

Trips to Tigre or Montevideo are separate options and are not part of the mandatory itinerary. In particular, **Montevideo** is in [Uruguay](/uruguay/), which is listed as a possible additional country but is not one of this tour's principal destinations.

## Program by stage

| Days | Activities |
|---|---|
| 1–4 | Rio and Carnival |
| 5–7 | Iguazu Falls |
| 8–10 | Buenos Aires |

The main itinerary includes four nights in Rio, two near Iguazu and three in Buenos Aires. Departure for home is scheduled for the final day.

## Price and included services

**The program price is $3725.** Included services comprise accommodation with breakfast, excursions with a Russian-speaking guide, scheduled transfers, tickets to the Carnival parade and the round-trip transfer to the Sambadrome.

International flights and domestic flights on the Rio–Iguazu–Buenos Aires route are paid separately, **from $450**. Optional excursions also have separate terms. For example, a trip to Tigre costs **$100 per person**, and a gaucho fiesta costs **$250 per person**. Montevideo is offered according to the chosen format, without one universal included price.

Meals and drinks during transfers are not included. It is important not to apply the conditions of optional excursions to the mandatory itinerary days: their pricing and content differ.

## Who will enjoy this tour?

The route is chosen for its combination of Carnival, natural attractions and Argentine culture. It is full of experiences and transfers. If a relaxed beach holiday is your priority, a program with a nighttime Sambadrome visit and several flights may feel too busy.

For comparison, see [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/), [multi-country journeys](/multi-country/) and our selection of [events and festivals trips](/interests/events-and-festivals/). Their content depends on actual dates, itineraries and optional services.

## Frequently asked questions about the Carnival tour

### Are Sambadrome tickets included in the price?

Yes. The included-services list specifies Carnival tickets and transfers between the hotel and the Sambadrome.

### Are both sides of Iguazu Falls visited?

Yes. The route covers the Brazilian and Argentine sides on separate excursion days.

### Is a visit to Uruguay included?

No. Montevideo is mentioned as an optional possibility with separate terms; the principal countries are Brazil and Argentina.
